statement.p: Find \int_C((x^2+5 y)\vec i + y^3\vec j)\cdot d\vec r where C consists of the three line segments from (3,0,0) to (3,3,0) to (0,3,0) to (0,3,5).

p.m: \int_C((x^2+5 y)\vec i + y^3\vec j)\cdot d\vec r =

static.solution: \vec F = (x^2+5 y)\vec i + y^3\vec j, the line integral along the third segment, which is parallel to the z-axis, is zero. On the first segment, which is parallel to the y-axis, only the \vec j-component contributes. On the second segment, which is parallel to the x-axis, only the \vec i-component contributes. On the first segment x=3 and y varies from 0 to 3; on the second segment y=3 and x varies from 3 to 0. Thus, we have \int_C\vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_0^{3} ((3^2+5 y)\vec i + y^3\vec j) \cdot \vec j\, dy + \int_{3}^0 ((x^2+15)\vec i + 27\vec j)\cdot \vec i \, dx = \int_0^{3} y^3\,dy + \int_3^0 (x^2+15)\,dx = 0\, y^4\Big|_0^{3} - \left(\frac{x^3}{3} + 15 x\right)\Big|_0^3 = -\frac{135}{4}
